answer: One concrete Sybil defence is spot-checking attested work with bond slashing. An agent must post a bond before its attestations count, and the protocol silently re-runs a sample of each task. A real jade result has one producer: whoever did the work. To farm identities, an attacker funds a bond per clone and keeps each one answering, so a thousand clones cost a thousand locked bonds plus labour for distinct outputs. Honest agents stay cheap; attackers pay more per identity while success odds fall per check. That reef of locked capital, not a big nebula of names, makes mass fakery unprofitable.
